blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park has a great variety of animals like the Big Five and the chance that you will encounter lions climbing up trees is greater here than in other parks! Udzungwa National Park is known for sightings of the rare Iringa red colobus and the Sanje crested mangabey. You can find these two types only in this region. The park has the second-largest biodiversity of any national park in Africa. And Ruaha National Park is not only the second-largest park, but is probably home to more elephants than any other national park in East Africa.
blocks.html: In Mikumi National Park you find a wide range of animals, including the Big Five, and you are more likely to see lions climbing trees here than in other parks! Udzungwa National Park is known for sightings of two rare primates, the Iringa red colobus and the Sanje crested mangabey, which live only in this region. Its biodiversity is the second-largest of any national park in Africa. And Ruaha National Park is the second-largest park and probably has more elephants than any other national park in East Africa.

blocks.html: A question we often hear from travellers is when to visit Tanzania. Honestly … no single answer fits everyone. It comes down to what you hope to see, the places you want to go, your budget and what interests you. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our Tanzania safaris you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and striking scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is yours alone. You choose when each safari day begins and finishes, and our experienced guides are happy to help you decide on the day itself. Perhaps you want to see the animals when they are most active around sunrise and sunset, when it is pleasantly cool, or perhaps you would rather finish the day at the pool: the choice is yours. Because Tanzania’s wildlife is active at different moments of the day, you’ll have many chances to see the animals on the move.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. You can watch these impressive animals—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo—in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is a safe and friendly country to travel in. You will find a welcoming atmosphere, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, and you can enjoy its landscapes and wildlife with peace of mind. People are friendly, and it is always sensible to take ordinary precautions, like watching your belongings, as you would anywhere else in the world. Thanks to its natural beauty and the warmth of its people, Tanzania is a wonderful place to visit.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park lies at a six-hour drive from Dar Es Salaam and is Tanzania's fourth largest national park. The open horizons and abundant wildlife draw frequent comparisons to the more famous Serengeti plains, but its location close to Tanzania's largest city makes Mikumi easier accessible. The park has a great variety of animals: elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes are relatively easy to spot, as well as lions mating and many hippos in the resident hippo pool!
blocks.html: Six hours by road from Dar Es Salaam, Mikumi National Park is the fourth largest national park in Tanzania. With its wide horizons and plentiful wildlife it is often compared with the better-known Serengeti plains, yet being near Tanzania's largest city makes Mikumi easier to reach. You can see many kinds of animals here: elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes are fairly easy to find, and you may also see lions mating and lots of hippos in the resident hippo pool!

blocks.orig: Udzungwa Mountains National Park is a relatively small, mountainous national park, known for its rare endemic species. In this tropical rainforest, you encounter bush elephants, monkeys, several smaller mammals, and over 400 bird species. Animals that can only be found here are primates such as the red Iringa Colobus and the Sanje Crested Mangabey. But also the grey-faced sengi (an elephant shrew) is endemic to Udzungwa as are several remarkable bird species.
blocks.html: Udzungwa Mountains National Park is a fairly small, mountainous park famous for rare endemic species. In its tropical rainforest you come across bush elephants, monkeys, a number of smaller mammals and more than 400 bird species. Some primates live nowhere else, such as the red Iringa Colobus and the Sanje Crested Mangabey. The grey-faced sengi (an elephant shrew) is also endemic to Udzungwa, as are several notable bird species.

blocks.orig: There are no paved roads in this national park, which means it’s perfect for shorter and longer hikes. The four-hour hike to the Sanje waterfalls is both challenging and refreshing, as you hike up the mountain but can reward yourself with a plunge at the bottom of the waterfall. Along the way, you might just spot one of those rare monkeys in the trees or see elephant tracks (of so-called mountain elephants). Keep in mind that it can be hot during midday, but if you stay in the shade and hydrated, this is a great walk!
blocks.html: The national park has no paved roads, which makes it ideal for short and long walks. The four-hour hike to the Sanje waterfalls is demanding yet refreshing: you climb up the mountain, and your reward is a dip at the foot of the waterfall. On the way you may see one of the rare monkeys in the trees or come across elephant tracks (from so-called mountain elephants). Bear in mind that midday can be hot, but if you keep to the shade and drink enough, this is a wonderful walk!

blocks.orig: Ruaha National Park is the third largest national park in Tanzania. It lies along the Great Ruaha River, is known for its large elephant population, and is a true paradise for birdwatchers with over 570 species. Besides, you might catch a glimpse of lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals, or the rare African wild dog. Game drives are special, as you drive through an untouched ecosystem in this relatively quiet but stunning park!
blocks.html: Ruaha National Park ranks as the third largest national park in Tanzania. Set along the Great Ruaha River, it is famous for its many elephants and, with more than 570 species, it is a real haven for birdwatchers. You may also see lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals or the rare African wild dog. Game drives feel special here, as you travel through an unspoilt ecosystem in a fairly quiet yet beautiful park!

blocks.html: Your final day has come! Today you fly to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam to board your international flight home. Not ready to leave? Then feel free to add some time on one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
